entries.title: Psalms 27:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Light - My counsellor in all my difficulties, and my comforter and deliverer in all my distresses. Strength - The supporter and preserver of my life.

entries.title: Psalms 27:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In this - That God is my light.

entries.title: Psalms 27:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Dwell. &100. - Have opportunity of constant attendance upon God. To behold - That there I may delight myself, in the contemplation of thy amiable and glorious majesty, and of thy infinite wisdom, holiness, justice, truth, and mercy.

entries.title: Psalms 27:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The secret - In his tabernacle, into which mine enemies cannot come. He alludes to the ancient custom of offenders, who used to flee to the tabernacle or altar. Rock - A place high and inaccessible.

entries.title: Psalms 27:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Away - From thy face or presence, or from the place of thy worship.

entries.title: Psalms 27:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Because of - That I may neither fall into their hands by my folly, nor give them any occasion of triumphing over me.

entries.title: Psalms 27:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The living - David was thus earnestly desirous of this mercy in this life, not because he placed his portion in these things; but because the truth and glory of God, were highly concerned in making good the promise of the kingdom to him.
